title: Florida House, District 115
what_it_does: Represents District 115 (Part of Miami-Dade) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: Omar Blanco
candidates.occupation: State representative; Miami-Dade County fire-rescue officer; former president of the Miami-Dade firefighters union (Local 1403)
candidates.background: Omar Blanco is a career Miami-Dade firefighter who previously led the Miami-Dade Firefighters and Paramedics union and ran for Congress in 2020. He won the open House District 115 seat in 2024 by about 19 points and is seeking a second term.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Blanco voted for HJR 203 (elimination of non-school homestead taxes) and for the HJR 1-F amendment on the 2026 ballot.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, CS/HJR 1-F (2026 special session), passage 75-26
Florida House roll call, CS/CS/HJR 203 (2026), passage 80-30

immigration.summary: Blanco voted for SB 2-C, the 2025 state immigration-enforcement package.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, SB 2-C (2025 special session, immigration), passage 85-30

guns.summary: He voted in 2025 and 2026 for bills lowering the long-gun purchase age from 21 to 18.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, HB 759 (2025, lower long-gun purchase age to 18), passage 78-34
Florida House roll call, HB 133 (2026, lower long-gun purchase age to 18), passage 74-37

taxes.summary: His 2024 platform prioritized keeping taxes low along with addressing insurance rates and public safety.

sources.title: The Floridian: Democrat Norma Perez Schwartz and Republican Omar Blanco faceoff for open HD 115 seat

crime.summary: He campaigned on enhancing public safety and supporting first responders.

candidates.name: Marcos Reyes
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.background: Marcos Reyes, 44, is a Cuban American small-business owner and the first in his family born in the United States. He ran for House District 119 in 2024, losing to Rep. Juan Carlos Porras, and chairs the credentials committee of the Miami-Dade Democratic Executive Committee.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

abortion.summary: Reyes says a woman's right to choose is important to him, citing his four daughters, and has called for codifying Roe v. Wade standards.
abortion.quote: A woman's right to choose is important to me. I have four daughters who will not have this right moving forward.

sources.title: Florida Choice Tracker: Marcos Reyes is Pro-Choice

other_issues.title: Cost of living and public education
other_issues.summary: In a June 2026 essay he said housing, insurance and grocery costs keep rising and that he wants to lower the cost of living and strengthen public education.

sources.title: Daily Kos: A Change in Florida is NEEDED! (by Marco Reyes)

other_issues.title: Cost of living and public education
other_issues.summary: In a post he wrote himself, Reyes said the cost of housing, insurance, groceries and everyday necessities keeps rising, and said he is running to put working families first, lower the cost of living, strengthen public education and end the Republican supermajority in the Legislature.

sources.title: A Change in Florida is NEEDED!
